newsitem.title: UK: Gripen on track at international show.
newsitem.headline: Gripen on track at international show.

text.p: The Swedish Air Force showed off its latest acquisition on Monday, the lightweight Gripen combat jet made by aerospace group Saab AB, the first time the company has been able to demonstrate an in-service plane to potential buyers.

Saab spokeswoman Pia Fores said the successful display flight at the Farnborough air show would help put the multi-role plane back on the international map after the embarrassment of a crash at a 1993 public display in Stockholm.
"It's good to show potential customers what it's capable of... We have solved the problems (from Stockholm)," she said.

So far the Gripen, whose maker is a unit of industrial combine Investor AB, has only been sold to the Swedish Air Force but it is being actively marketed as the first of a new generation of combat aircraft to enter service.
Saab's marketing presence received an extra boost at this huge biennial air show thanks to high-profile facilities provided by its new partner British Aerospace Plc Plc.

BAe and Saab are already cooperating in the Gripen's production and Fores said that the definition of a jointly- developed baseline standard for export aircraft should be ready towards the end of this year.
Industry sources say the Gripen is seeking consideration for requirements in Austria, Hungary, Poland and Chile.
Fores said Saab and BAe see the export market opening up fully after 2000 when more countries start looking to replace ageing conventional fighters.

Gripen was one of three of the latest generation of high- tech warplanes to fly at Farnborough. The four-nation Eurofighter, a bigger and heavier air superiority fighter, and the French Rafale, made by Dassault, were also due to perform.

Planes like Gripen, Eurofighter, and the U.S.-made F-22, derive extreme levels of agility from their aerodynamically unstable construction which can only be piloted with the aid of sophisticated computer flight control systems.
